answer: A hosted mining economy resists Sybil attacks by making each identity stake a bonded deposit that is slashed when collusion is detected, and by routing rewards only to identities whose work history spans a shared chain. A Sybil farm cannot spread one capital pool across cheap accounts, because every new tundra of fresh identities, an island with no track record, must independently lock the same stake before earning anything. The thread linking accounts to past payouts makes siblings visible, so the operator pays the stake again per fake node and risks losing all of it at once.
